name: Astronómia - základy
description: Základné pojmy z astronómie a fyzikálnych veličín spojených s týmto odborom
author: Techdoc, Ltd.

words.definition: A small rocky body orbiting the Sun.

contextSentences.en: The asteroid 2004 BL86 flew past Earth at a distance of about 1.2 million kilometres.
Scientists study the composition of asteroids to learn about the early solar system.

words.example_en: The asteroid passed close to Earth last night.
words.example_sk: Asteroid preletel včera v noci tesne okolo Zeme.

words.definition: The layer of gases surrounding a planet or star.

contextSentences.en: The Earth's atmosphere is divided into several layers, including the troposphere and stratosphere.
Without a protective atmosphere, the surface of a planet is exposed to harmful radiation.

words.example_en: The thick atmosphere of Venus traps heat effectively.
words.example_sk: Hustá atmosféra Venuše účinne zadržiava teplo.

words.definition: A region in space where gravity is so strong that nothing can escape.

contextSentences.en: The first ever image of a black hole was captured and released in 2019.
Nothing, not even light, can escape the gravitational pull of a black hole.

words.example_en: Light cannot escape from a black hole.
words.example_sk: Svetlo nemôže uniknúť z čiernej diery.

words.definition: An icy object in space that forms a bright tail near the Sun.

contextSentences.en: Halley's comet is visible from Earth roughly every 75 years.
As the comet approached the Sun, it developed a bright, glowing tail.

words.example_en: A bright comet appeared in the night sky.
words.example_sk: Na nočnej oblohe sa objavila jasná kométa.

words.definition: A group of stars forming a recognised pattern.

contextSentences.en: The constellation Orion is one of the easiest to spot in the winter night sky.
Ancient sailors used the positions of constellations to navigate at sea.

words.example_en: Orion is a constellation visible in winter.
words.example_sk: Orion je súhvezdie viditeľné v zime.

words.definition: An event in which one celestial body moves into the shadow of another.

contextSentences.en: During a total solar eclipse, the Moon completely blocks the Sun's light.
A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon.

words.example_en: We wore special glasses to watch the solar eclipse.
words.example_sk: Na pozorovanie slnečného zatmenia sme si nasadili špeciálne okuliare.

words.definition: A huge system of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.

contextSentences.en: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, contains an estimated 200 to 400 billion stars.
The Andromeda galaxy is the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way.

words.example_en: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, contains billions of stars.
words.example_sk: Naša galaxia, Mliečna dráha, obsahuje miliardy hviezd.

words.definition: The force that attracts objects toward each other.

contextSentences.en: Gravity keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun and the Moon around the Earth.
Albert Einstein described gravity as a curvature of space and time.

words.example_en: Gravity pulls the ball back to the ground.
words.example_sk: Gravitácia pritahuje loptičku späť k zemi.

words.definition: Relating to the Moon.

contextSentences.en: The lunar surface is covered with craters formed by meteorite impacts.
The lunar cycle lasts approximately 29.5 days and influences ocean tides.

words.example_en: The astronauts collected lunar rocks during the mission.
words.example_sk: Astronauti počas misie nazbierali lunárne kamene.

words.definition: A piece of rock from space that burns brightly in the atmosphere.

contextSentences.en: During the Perseid meteor shower, hundreds of meteors can be seen in a single night.
A meteor burns up as it enters the Earth's atmosphere, creating a streak of light.

words.example_en: We saw a meteor streak across the sky.
words.example_sk: Videli sme, ako po oblohe preletel meteor.

words.definition: A cloud of gas and dust in outer space.

contextSentences.en: The Orion Nebula is a region of active star formation visible to the naked eye.
Nebulae are vast clouds of gas and dust that serve as the birthplaces of new stars.

words.example_en: The Orion Nebula is a vast cloud of gas and dust.
words.example_sk: Mlhovina Orion je obrovský oblak plynu a prachu.

words.definition: The curved path of an object around a star, planet, or moon.

contextSentences.en: The International Space Station completes one orbit of the Earth every 90 minutes.
The Moon travels in a slightly elliptical orbit around the Earth.

words.example_en: The Moon stays in orbit around Earth.
words.example_sk: Mesiac obieha okolo Zeme.

words.definition: A large round object in space that moves around a star.

contextSentences.en: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with a mass greater than all others combined.
Since 2006, Pluto has been classified as a dwarf planet rather than a full planet.

words.example_en: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.
words.example_sk: Mars je štvrtá planéta od Slnka.

words.definition: The Sun and all the objects that orbit it.

contextSentences.en: Our solar system formed roughly 4.6 billion years ago from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft has left the solar system and is now travelling through interstellar space.

words.example_en: The solar system includes the Sun and eight planets.
words.example_sk: Slnko a osem planét tvoria slnečnú sústavu.

words.definition: An instrument used to observe distant objects in space.

contextSentences.en: Galileo Galilei was among the first to use a telescope for astronomical observations.
The James Webb Space Telescope provides the most detailed images of the early universe ever taken.

words.example_en: She used a telescope to observe Saturn's rings.
words.example_sk: Pomocou ďalekohľadu pozorovala Saturnovy prstence.

words.definition: Relating to the sky, outer space, or the objects found in it.
words.example_en: Through the observatory dome, we watched several celestial objects drift across the night sky before dawn.
words.example_sk: Cez kupolu observatória sme pred úsvitom sledovali, ako sa po nočnej oblohe pohybuje niekoľko nebeských objektov.

contextSentences.en: Ancient astronomers carefully recorded celestial events such as eclipses and comet appearances.

words.definition: A large bowl-shaped hollow on the surface of the Earth, the Moon, or another planet, often caused by an impact or volcanic activity.
words.example_en: The meteor left a huge crater in the desert.
words.example_sk: Meteorit zanechal v púšti obrovský kráter.

words.definition: An imaginary line circling a planet at equal distance from the poles, dividing it into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
words.example_en: The airplane crossed the equator during the flight.
words.example_sk: Lietadlo preletelo cez rovník počas letu.

words.definition: Existing or occurring among or between the stars.
words.example_en: Although scientists dream of interstellar travel, reaching another star system remains science fiction.
words.example_sk: Hoci vedci snívajú o medziplanetárnych cestách, dosiahnutie inej hviezdnej sústavy zostáva zatiaľ len sci-fi.

words.definition: A natural or artificial body that orbits a larger body in space, such as a moon orbiting a planet or a man-made object used for communication, navigation, or observation.
words.example_en: Scientists launched a new satellite to study Earth's atmosphere.
words.example_sk: Vedci vypustili nový satelit, aby skúmal atmosféru Zeme.

words.definition: A range or band of related values, qualities, or ideas; specifically, the continuous sequence of colors produced when light is dispersed, or the distribution of electromagnetic radiation by wavelength or frequency.
words.example_en: A prism splits white light into a spectrum of colors.
words.example_sk: Hranol rozloží biele svetlo na spektrum farieb.

words.definition: A large spacecraft designed for travel between stars, especially as depicted in science fiction.
words.example_en: The crew boarded the starship for their journey to the distant system.
words.example_sk: Posádka nastúpila na hviezdnu loď na cestu do vzdialeného systému.

words.definition: All space, time, matter, and energy that exist.
words.example_en: Scientists study how the universe began.
words.example_sk: Vedci skúmajú, ako vznikol vesmír.

words.definition: The highest point reached by something, especially the sun or a celestial body in the sky; the peak or greatest success of something.
words.example_en: Her career reached its zenith in the early 2000s.
words.example_sk: Jej kariéra dosiahla svoj zenit na začiatku 21. storočia.

words.definition: Either of the two times in the year when the day and night are of approximately equal length, occurring in spring and autumn.
words.example_en: The spring equinox marks the beginning of astronomical spring.
words.example_sk: Jarná rovnodennosť označuje začiatok astronomickej jari.

words.definition: Either of the two times of the year when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point in the sky at noon, marking the longest and shortest days.
words.example_en: The summer solstice is the longest day of the year.
words.example_sk: Letný slnovrat je najdlhší deň v roku.

words.definition: The distance that light travels in one year, used especially in astronomy.
words.example_en: The nearest star to the Sun is about 4.24 light-years away.
words.example_sk: Najbližšia hviezda k Slnku je vzdialená asi 4,24 svetelného roka.

words.definition: A star explosion that suddenly becomes extremely bright and releases a large amount of energy.
words.example_en: Astronomers observed a supernova in a distant galaxy.
words.example_sk: Astronómovia pozorovali supernovu vo vzdialenej galaxii.

words.definition: The path followed by an object moving through space or the air.
words.example_en: The scientists calculated the trajectory of the rocket.
words.example_sk: Vedci vypočítali trajektóriu rakety.

words.definition: The act or process of turning around a central point or axis.
words.example_en: The rotation of the Earth causes day and night.
words.example_sk: Rotácia Zeme spôsobuje deň a noc.

words.definition: A building or place equipped for observing astronomical, meteorological, or other natural phenomena.
words.example_en: We visited the observatory to look at the stars through a large telescope.
words.example_sk: Navštívili sme observatórium, aby sme sa pozreli na hviezdy cez veľký teleskop.

words.definition: A scientist who studies stars, planets, and other objects in space.
words.example_en: The astronomer used a telescope to observe distant galaxies.
words.example_sk: Astronóm použil teleskop na pozorovanie vzdialených galaxií.

words.definition: A real or imaginary straight line around which something turns or is arranged.
words.example_en: The Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours.
words.example_sk: Zem sa otočí okolo svojej osi raz za 24 hodín.

words.definition: One half of the Earth, the brain, or another sphere.
words.example_en: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.
words.example_sk: Austrália sa nachádza na južnej pologuli.

words.definition: Energy that travels through space or a substance in the form of waves or particles.
words.example_en: Too much exposure to radiation can be harmful to your health.
words.example_sk: Príliš veľké vystavenie žiareniu môže byť škodlivé pre tvoje zdravie.

words.definition: A space completely empty of matter; also a machine used for cleaning by suction, or the act of cleaning with such a machine.
words.example_en: The chamber was emptied of air to create a vacuum.
words.example_sk: Použila vysávač na vyčistenie koberca.

words.definition: A large amount of matter or substance; the amount of matter in an object; in another meaning, a religious service in some Christian churches.
words.example_en: The box has a mass of 10 kilograms.
words.example_sk: Krabica má hmotnosť 10 kilogramov.

words.definition: The height of an object or place above sea level or above the ground.
words.example_en: The plane flew at an altitude of 10,000 meters.
words.example_sk: Lietadlo letelo v nadmorskej výške 10 000 metrov.

words.definition: The region of space far beyond the Earth and its atmosphere, especially far from the solar system or from human activity.
words.example_en: Scientists use powerful telescopes to study deep space.
words.example_sk: Vedci používajú výkonné teleskopy na skúmanie hlbokého vesmíru.
